rows.english: If one focusses primarily on the taking of vows, and then fails in the practical aspects of keeping them seriously and restoring them when they are damaged, then there is absolutely no way that one's practice of the ethical way of life can be pure. As such it is essential that you now go on to help your new monks keep their vows well by learning to identify what constitutes breaking them. So too you must institute a regular practice of purification and restoration, whereby the monks learn to confess past errors and restrain themselves from future error, in the event that--because of one of the four factors, such as not understanding the vows properly--they should ever transgress them. They must learn never to take it lightly when they break a vow; they must be taught the proper methods of restoring vows in every instance where they are broken. In this way, and through developing a sense of shame and propriety, as well as watchfulness, awareness, and similar tools, they will come to lead a perfectly ethical way of life.

rows.english: As we just noted, it has been spoken that even those beings who are flies and gnats, or bees, and even those who live as worms as well can reach unmatched enlightenment, which is so difficult to reach, if they "develop the force of effort"; which is to say, if they amass the necessary good karma. We can thus think to ourselves, And then there is someone like me, someone born as a member of a kind of being which is truly extraordinary: I have been born human. And I possess as well an extraordinary mental ability; that is, I can tell what will help or what will hurt me in my pursuit of the state of enlightenment. Assuming then that I never give up the bodhisattva's way of life--which is to say, assuming that I can continue to practice the activities which bodhisattvas do continually--why shouldn't I reach enlightenment? Of course I can. Contemplation Eleven The courage of no choice

rows.english: Nor even is it that--without the words having come out of our mouths--we bring to mind the form they would take once they have come out, and then consider the winds as being inseparable from this outer song.  Rather, the way that we do our recitation of the diamonds at this point is that we think of the three sacred syllables as sounding out themselves in the way that they sing their song within the channels, as the winds run there.  We first acquaint ourselves with what this would sound like, and then focus our minds on this sound without allow the mind to be distracted in any way to something else.

rows.wylie: gsum pa ya nga ba spang zhing sgyu mar bslab pa la ya nga ba spang ba ni, rmi lam gyi dus su me dang chu la sogs pa'i ya nga ba 'am bag tsha ba byung na, rmi lam du ngo shes par byas nas, rmi lam gyi me dang chu la sogs pas gnod par ga la 'gyur snyam du bsams la, mchod pa dang, brgal ba la sogs pa'i thogs brdzis bya'o
rows.english: Next comes our third section, on eliminating fears in your dreams and learning about the illusion.  The unusual Tibetan word ya-ngawa here refers to fears, or various frightening visions that you have in your dreams, such as great fires or floods or the like.  Here you have to learn to recognize them as part of a dream: to reach a point where you can say, "Now how could things like a fire or a flood in my dreams ever hurt me?" And then you learn how to avoid them in your dreams, by making offerings, or crossing over them, or through other such ways.

rows.english: Here is how you learn about the illusion.  Now it's one thing to learn to recognize a dream as a dream: to realize that the things in your dreams that look like a water pitcher or a bolt of cloth or the like are actually devoid of any nature of being these things at all.  This in itself though is not what it means when we say you have realized that the dream has no nature of its own.

rows.acip: GNYID DUS SU GNYID JI LTAR 'THUG KYANG 'OD GSAL DANG BSRE THUB NA, RLUNG STOBS KYIS DA GZOD 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL MA BU BSRE NUS, 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL LA DER NGO SHES NAS BSRE NUS NA, DE'I PHYI LOGS SU BAR DO 'CHAR BA NGO SHES PAS, BAR DO ZIN PA'I THABS DAM PA NI, 'CHI BA'I 'OD GSAL NGOS ZIN NAS BSRE NUS PA YIN GYI, DE LAS GZHAN MED DO,,
rows.wylie: gnyid dus su gnyid ji ltar 'thug kyang 'od gsal dang bsre thub na, rlung stobs kyis da gzod 'chi ba'i 'od gsal ma bu bsre nus, 'chi ba'i 'od gsal la der ngo shes nas bsre nus na, de'i phyi logs su bar do 'char ba ngo shes pas, bar do zin pa'i thabs dam pa ni, 'chi ba'i 'od gsal ngos zin nas bsre nus pa yin gyi, de las gzhan med do
rows.english: If you reach a point during your sleep period where you can blend your sleep with the clear light regardless of how deep your sleep is, then you be that much better able to blend the mother and child clear light of death, by force of the condition of your winds.  And if you can get to a point where you can recognize the clear light of death for what it is, and blend it, then as soon as it ends and the intermediate state begins you can also recognize it for what it is.  As such, the very highest method for achieving recognition of the intermediate state is being able to recognize the clear light of death and then blend it: there is nothing else like it.

rows.wylie: de lta'i 'chi ba 'od gsal las ldang bar rtsom pa na, yid ngor lha'i skur ldang bar mi nus kyang , bar do'i snang ba shar ba na, bar do la bar do yin par ngo shes par byas nas bar do'i lus longs sku rnal 'byor ma'i skur bsgom pa ste de ni 'chi dus kyi longs sku'i bsre ba
rows.english: When the time comes for you to begin rising out of this kind of death clear light, it may not be possible for you to see yourself rising up in the holy Body of an Angel.  Nonetheless, when you start to appear to yourself as a being between death and rebirth, you should recognize this inbetween being as an inbetween being.  At this point you should meditate that the body of this inbetween being is the sacred body of the Holy Angel in her enjoyment body.  This then is (2) the blending of the enjoyment body during the period of dying.
